summary: Bernard Williams was a philosopher who studied at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He later held academic posts at University College London (~1962–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian who held posts at the University of Oldenburg (~1987–1992) and Heidelberg University (~2003).

Bernfried Schlerath worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under Paul Thieme (~1952–1956) and held positions at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1956–1965), the University of Marburg (~1965–1974), and the Free University of Berlin (~1974–1992).
Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist who served as a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1938–1945), where he succeeded Heinrich Lüders.

Bernhard Forssman specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1959–1964), and held posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger worked in Indology and Iranian studies. He studied at Vienna, Bonn, Charles, Göttingen, and Heidelberg, learning under Leopold von Schroeder and Franz Kielhorn. He taught at Vienna (~1909–1938), the Iranian Institute (1938–1951), and Columbia University (1951–1953).

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at Zurich, under Franz Bopp at Berlin (~1830–1832), Göttingen (~1832–1833), and Paris (~1833–1835). He held posts as reader, Dozent, and Privatdozent at the University of Zurich between 1833 and 1845.

Bernhard Karlgren was a scholar of sinology and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1909) and later held academic posts at Uppsala (~1913–1915) and the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Bernhard Kölver worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne, he held posts at Cologne, the Nepal Research Centre, Kiel University (1974–1993), and Leipzig University as professor of Indology (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman was a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher. He earned degrees from NYU and UCLA, and studied under traditional teachers Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers (1980).

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford, completing her PhD under Jonathan A. Silk in 2010. She held posts at Heidelberg University (~2015) and Leiden University (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Halle and Berlin under Pott, Weber, Haym, Bopp, and Steinthal. He served as Privatdozent at Halle (1867–1870) and held a chair at the University of Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer worked in Tibetology, Sinology, and Iranian studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady and others. He held positions at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, and the Field Museum of Natural History (1907).

Beru Khyentse Rinpoche II is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khunu Rinpoche, Sakya Trizin, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied across Salzburg, Vienna, Zurich, Rome, and Munich. Her career includes posts at Banaras Hindu University, the Alice Boner Institute, the University of Vienna, and the Abhinavagupta Research Library.

Betty Heimann worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen, Bonn, Strasbourg, Kiel, and Halle under teachers including Simmel, Deussen, Sieg, and Hultzsch. She held posts at Halle, Hamburg (1931–1933), London, Oxford, and Colombo (1945–1949).
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and as Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Murray Barnson Emeneau at the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad (1986–1999).

Bhagavan Das was an Indian scholar in philosophy and Indology who graduated with an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He served as Honorary Secretary at Banaras Hindu University (~1916–1921) and headmaster at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1921–1926).

Bhagwan Dash was a scholar in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi (~1971–1978). He worked as a bibliographer and cataloguer for the Library of Congress.
